data.name: Bench.Rt.NotReady
data.value: This card has DXR 1.1, but the ray tracing test is not available in this version yet: it could not be validated without a ray tracing card to check the image and the score.

data.name: Bench.Rt.NoDirect3D12
data.value: Direct3D 12 did not respond on this PC, so ray tracing could not be checked.

data.name: Stress.Gpu.WindowNote
data.value: A window with the load opens in front. Esc or closing the window also stops the test.

data.name: Diag.Events.ShowNoise.Detail
data.value: Events that show up thousands of times or that Windows considers harmless are hidden by default.

data.name: Diag.Events.Hidden
data.value: {0} repetitive events hidden, from {1} kind(s). Turn on “Show repeated noise” to see them.

data.name: Diag.Events.Empty
data.value: No relevant errors or warnings in this period.

data.name: Diag.Events.Truncated
data.value: The period has too many events; the reading stopped at the newest ones of each log.

data.name: Diag.Known.KernelPower41.Title
data.value: The PC shut down without warning

data.name: Diag.Known.KernelPower41.Detail
data.value: Windows restarted without a clean shutdown: power loss, freeze, forced restart or blue screen. If it happens on its own, check temperatures, power supply and memory.

data.name: Diag.Known.UnexpectedShutdown6008.Detail
data.value: Windows logs this on the boot after an unclean shutdown. It usually comes with the Kernel-Power 41 event.

data.name: Diag.Known.BugCheck1001.Title
data.value: Windows restarted after a blue screen

data.name: Diag.Known.BugCheck1001.Detail
data.value: The Blue screens page shows the code and what it usually means.

data.name: Diag.Known.DiskBadBlock.Detail
data.value: The disk reported a bad block. One can be normal; if it repeats, back up and check SMART on the Storage page.

data.name: Diag.Known.DiskController.Detail
data.value: The disk, the cable or the controller failed on an operation. If it repeats, it points to the cable, the SATA port or the disk itself.

data.name: Diag.Known.DiskPaging.Detail
data.value: Windows could not read or write virtual memory on the disk. It points to a disk or memory problem.

data.name: Diag.Known.DiskRetried.Detail
data.value: Windows had to repeat a read or write. A few times is normal; many in a short time point to a failing disk or cable.

data.name: Diag.Known.NtfsCorruption.Detail
data.value: NTFS found corruption. Run the disk check on the Repair page and back up.

data.name: Diag.Known.NvmeReset.Detail
data.value: Windows had to reset the SSD because it was slow to answer. If it repeats, update the SSD firmware and driver.

data.name: Diag.Known.DisplayTimeout.Title
data.value: The graphics driver stopped responding and recovered

data.name: Diag.Known.DisplayTimeout.Detail
data.value: Usually an unstable graphics driver, overclock or high card temperature. If it repeats, reinstall the driver and test without overclock.

data.name: Diag.Known.DriverNotLoaded.Detail
data.value: Windows could not start a device driver. If the device works you can ignore it; otherwise reinstall the driver.

data.name: Diag.Known.TpmProvisioning.Title
data.value: The TPM was not fully provisioned

data.name: Diag.Known.TpmProvisioning.Detail
data.value: Common warning on desktop PCs. It only matters if you need the TPM, for example for Windows 11 or BitLocker.

data.name: Diag.Known.DcomPermission.Detail
data.value: Very common and almost always harmless: a Windows program asked for a permission it does not have. You can ignore it.

data.name: Diag.Known.DcomNoResponse.Title
data.value: A DCOM server did not respond

data.name: Diag.Known.DcomNoResponse.Detail
data.value: A program tried to talk to a component that did not answer in time. It only matters if it comes with freezes.

data.name: Diag.Known.EsentFile.Title
data.value: A Windows database complaining about a file

data.name: Diag.Known.EsentFile.Detail
data.value: It usually comes from search or another Windows service and repeats thousands of times. Generally harmless, and hidden by default.

data.name: Diag.Known.TimeSync.Title
data.value: The clock could not sync with the time server

data.name: Diag.Known.TimeSync.Detail
data.value: It may be the internet being unstable at the time. If the PC clock ends up wrong, change the Windows time server.

data.name: Diag.Known.ServiceFailedToStart.Detail
data.value: The event text says which one. If it is a service you use, restart it; if it belongs to a program you uninstalled, it is a leftover.

data.name: Diag.Known.ServiceTimeout.Title
data.value: A service took too long to respond

data.name: Diag.Known.ServiceTimeout.Detail
data.value: Windows gave up waiting for the service. It tends to happen at boot, when the PC is busy.

data.name: Diag.Known.ServiceTerminated.Detail
data.value: The service stopped on its own. If it is important, check the Services page.

data.name: Diag.Known.ServiceCrashed.Detail
data.value: The service closed with an error. If it repeats, reinstall the program that owns it.

data.name: Diag.Known.FilterAttach.Title
data.value: A file filter could not attach to a volume

data.name: Diag.Known.FilterAttach.Detail
data.value: Common with antivirus, backup or virtual disk drivers. Harmless if nothing else fails.

data.name: Diag.Known.VssError.Detail
data.value: It affects restore points and backups. Check that system protection is on.

data.name: Diag.Known.VolsnapError.Title
data.value: Failed to create a volume shadow copy

data.name: Diag.Known.VolsnapError.Detail
data.value: It can affect restore points. Lack of disk space is the most common cause.

data.name: Diag.Known.AppCrash.Detail
data.value: The event text shows which program and module failed. The same program repeating calls for an update or a reinstall.

data.name: Diag.Known.DotNetCrash.Title
data.value: A .NET program closed on an error

data.name: Diag.Known.DotNetCrash.Detail
data.value: An app built on .NET hit an error it did not handle. The event text shows which one.

data.name: Diag.Known.AppHang.Detail
data.value: The program froze its window and Windows logged it. If repeated, it calls for an update or a reinstall.

data.name: Diag.Known.AppReport.Detail
data.value: It goes with a program failure and carries the report file name.

data.name: Diag.Known.UpdateFailed.Detail
data.value: Try again in Settings, Windows Update. If it persists, the Repair page has the Windows Update repairs.

data.name: Diag.Known.Whea.Detail
data.value: The processor, the memory or the PCI bus reported an error. Corrected now and then is normal; repeated or fatal deserves attention: check temperature, overclock and memory.

data.name: Diag.Known.GpuDriver.Detail
data.value: The graphics card driver logged a problem. If it comes with screen freezes, reinstall the driver and test without overclock.

data.name: Diag.Known.Perflib.Detail
data.value: A program installed faulty performance counters. Harmless.

data.name: Diag.Crashes.Settings.AutoReboot
data.value: Restart on its own after a blue screen

data.name: Diag.Crashes.Settings.Advice.Off
data.value: This PC is set to keep nothing when a blue screen happens. Without that, a blue screen shows up as just an unexpected restart, with no code and no cause. To turn it on: Windows Settings, System, About, Advanced system settings, Startup and Recovery, and choose “Automatic memory dump”.

data.name: Diag.Crashes.Settings.Advice.Unknown
data.value: Windows has no dump type set on this PC. Check Startup and Recovery in the advanced system settings.

data.name: Diag.Crashes.Shutdowns.Empty
data.value: No unexpected restarts in this period.

data.name: Diag.Crashes.Cause.BlueScreen.NoDescription
data.value: Windows has no description for this code. Search for it together with “bug check” to see what it means.

data.name: Diag.Crashes.Cause.PowerButton
data.value: Forced shutdown with the power button

data.name: Diag.Crashes.Cause.PowerButton.Detail
data.value: The power button was held until the PC turned off. It is usually the way out of a frozen screen.

data.name: Diag.Crashes.Cause.Unknown.Detail
data.value: It may have been a power loss, a total freeze or a blue screen that left no record. If the PC restarts on its own, check the power supply, temperatures and memory.

data.name: Diag.Crashes.Apps.Empty
data.value: No program crashed in this period.

data.name: Diag.Crashes.Origin.GraphicsDriver
data.value: The module that failed is the {0} graphics driver. If it repeats, reinstall the driver (cleaning the old one) and test without overclock.

data.name: Diag.Crashes.Origin.Windows
data.value: The module that failed belongs to Windows itself. If it repeats, the Repair page helps fix system files.

data.name: Diag.Crashes.Origin.Application
data.value: The error is in the program's own code. Updating or reinstalling usually fixes it.

data.name: Diag.Crashes.Origin.ThirdPartyModule
data.value: The module that failed is third-party (a plugin, overlay or library). Turning off whatever hooks into that program usually fixes it.

data.name: Diag.Crashes.KernelDumps.Empty
data.value: No blue screen dump files on this PC.

data.name: Diag.Crashes.UserDumps.Hint
data.value: Files Windows keeps when a program crashes. They can take a lot of space and contain the program's data.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL.Detail
data.value: A driver or the kernel touched memory at the wrong time. Usually a faulty driver or unstable memory.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.BAD_POOL_HEADER.Detail
data.value: System memory was corrupted. It points to a bad driver or faulty memory.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.MEMORY_MANAGEMENT.Detail
data.value: Serious memory management error. Run the Windows memory diagnostic and test the sticks one by one.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.KMODE_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED.Detail
data.value: A driver raised an error nobody handled. Update or reinstall the driver of the device named in the dump.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.NTFS_FILE_SYSTEM.Detail
data.value: The file system hit an error. Check the disk on the Repair page and back up.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.SYSTEM_SERVICE_EXCEPTION.Detail
data.value: A system service failed, almost always because of the graphics driver or antivirus. Reinstall the graphics driver.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.NO_MORE_SYSTEM_PTES.Detail
data.value: Windows ran out of kernel address space because of a driver leak. Update the drivers.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.PFN_LIST_CORRUPT.Detail
data.value: The memory page list was corrupted. It points to a bad driver or faulty memory.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA.Detail
data.value: The system tried to use memory that does not exist. Usually faulty memory, a bad driver or a failing disk.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.REGISTRY_ERROR.Detail
data.value: Windows found a problem in the registry or on the disk that holds it. Check the disk.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.KERNEL_STACK_INPAGE_ERROR.Detail
data.value: Windows could not read data from disk into memory. It points to a disk, cable or controller problem.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR.Detail
data.value: Windows could not read data from disk into memory. It points to a disk, cable or controller problem.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE.Detail
data.value: Windows lost access to the boot disk. It happens after changing the controller mode (AHCI/RAID) or a storage driver.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.SYSTEM_THREAD_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED.Detail
data.value: A system task failed unhandled, almost always because of a driver. The dump says which one.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.UNEXPECTED_KERNEL_MODE_TRAP.Detail
data.value: The CPU received a condition the kernel did not expect. It can be memory, overheating or an unstable overclock.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE.Detail
data.value: A driver did not answer when suspending or waking the device. Update the drivers and check the power options.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.INTERNAL_POWER_ERROR.Detail
data.value: Internal power management error. Update the BIOS and the chipset drivers.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.ACPI_BIOS_ERROR.Detail
data.value: The BIOS described the hardware in a way Windows does not accept. Update the BIOS.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.ATTEMPTED_WRITE_TO_READONLY_MEMORY.Detail
data.value: A driver tried to write to protected memory. Update or reinstall the driver named in the dump.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.BAD_POOL_CALLER.Detail
data.value: A driver asked for memory the wrong way. Update the drivers and remove any you installed recently.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.DRIVER_VERIFIER_DETECTED_VIOLATION.Detail
data.value: Driver Verifier caught a driver doing something forbidden. Turn the verifier off if you did not turn it on.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.DRIVER_CORRUPTED_EXPOOL.Detail
data.value: A driver corrupted system memory. Update the drivers.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL.Detail
data.value: A driver accessed memory at a forbidden moment. It is one of the most common codes; the dump points to the driver.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.THREAD_STUCK_IN_DEVICE_DRIVER.Detail
data.value: A driver, usually the graphics one, got stuck waiting for the hardware. Reinstall the graphics driver.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED.Detail
data.value: An essential Windows process ended. It can be the disk, memory or damaged system files.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.CRITICAL_OBJECT_TERMINATION.Detail
data.value: An essential process or thread ended. It can be the disk, memory or damaged system files.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.CLOCK_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT.Detail
data.value: A CPU core stopped responding. Usually an unstable overclock or undervolt, or an outdated BIOS.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.CRITICAL_STRUCTURE_CORRUPTION.Detail
data.value: The kernel detected that a protected structure was changed. It can be a bad driver or faulty memory.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE.Detail
data.value: The graphics driver stopped responding and Windows could not recover. Reinstall the driver and test without overclock.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.VIDEO_TDR_TIMEOUT_DETECTED.Detail
data.value: The graphics card took too long to respond. Reinstall the driver and test without overclock.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.VIDEO_SCHEDULER_INTERNAL_ERROR.Detail
data.value: The video scheduler hit a fatal error. Reinstall the graphics driver.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR.Detail
data.value: The hardware reported an error that could not be corrected: CPU, memory, motherboard or overclock. Check temperatures and test without overclock.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION.Detail
data.value: A driver took too long on an urgent task. Usually an SSD, network or graphics driver; update the SSD firmware.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE.Detail
data.value: The kernel detected corrupted data. It can be a bad driver, memory or a failing disk.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.KERNEL_MODE_HEAP_CORRUPTION.Detail
data.value: A driver corrupted kernel memory. Update the drivers.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.VIDEO_ENGINE_TIMEOUT_DETECTED.Detail
data.value: A graphics card engine stopped responding. Reinstall the graphics driver and check the card temperature.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.UNEXPECTED_STORE_EXCEPTION.Detail
data.value: The Windows storage component hit an error. Usually a failing SSD or disk driver; check SMART.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.LIVE_SYSTEM_DUMP.Detail
data.value: This is not a blue screen: Windows took a copy of memory without shutting the PC down, because of a problem that did not bring the system down.

data.name: Diag.BugCheck.SYNTHETIC_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT.Detail
data.value: The system stayed frozen for too long without answering. Usually a driver, overclock or BIOS.

data.name: Diag.Exception.BREAKPOINT.Detail
data.value: The program stopped at a breakpoint, which happens with debuggers or an internal error.

data.name: Diag.Exception.ACCESS_VIOLATION.Detail
data.value: Invalid memory access, the most common reason for a crash.

data.name: Diag.Exception.ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION.Detail
data.value: The program ran an instruction the CPU does not know, like a new program on an old CPU.

data.name: Diag.Exception.INT_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO.Detail
data.value: Division by zero inside the program.

data.name: Diag.Exception.STACK_OVERFLOW.Detail
data.value: The program used more stack than exists, usually because of an endless recursion.

data.name: Diag.Exception.DLL_NOT_FOUND.Detail
data.value: The program needs a DLL that was not found. Reinstall the program or the Visual C++ components.

data.name: Diag.Exception.DLL_INIT_FAILED.Detail
data.value: A DLL failed to start. It can be the wrong version or a broken component.

data.name: Diag.Exception.HEAP_CORRUPTION.Detail
data.value: The program's memory was corrupted. Usually a program bug or an injected module.

data.name: Diag.Exception.STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN.Detail
data.value: The program ended on a security check or a fatal internal error.

data.name: Diag.Exception.INVALID_IMAGE_FORMAT.Detail
data.value: The program or a DLL has a mismatched architecture (32 and 64 bits mixed).

data.name: Diag.Exception.CLR_EXCEPTION.Detail
data.value: A .NET program threw an exception it did not handle.

data.name: Diag.Exception.CPP_EXCEPTION.Detail
data.value: A C++ program threw an exception it did not handle.

data.name: Diag.Reliability.Chart.Name
data.value: Stability index over the period; now {0} out of 10

data.name: Diag.Reliability.Chart.Note
data.value: Windows works out the index every hour, from 1 to 10, from the failures of the last days. Each failure drops the number and it only climbs back after days without failures. The red ticks at the bottom mark when failures happened.

data.name: Diag.Reliability.ShowChanges.Detail
data.value: By default the list shows only failures, which are what lowers the index.

data.name: Diag.Reliability.Hidden
data.value: {0} records that are not failures (installs, updates and others) are hidden. Turn on the switch above to see them.

data.name: Diag.Reliability.Empty
data.value: No failures recorded in this period.

data.name: Diag.Logs.Search
data.value: Search the text, the source and the details

data.name: Diag.Logs.Showing
data.value: Showing the {0} newest of {1} entries that match the filter.

data.name: Diag.Logs.MidFile
data.value: The file is large; only its end was read.

data.name: Diag.Logs.NoFiles
data.value: There are no log files yet.

data.name: Diag.Logs.CopyFailed
data.value: Windows did not let the clipboard be used right now. Try again.

data.name: Diag.Report.Footer
data.value: Generated on this computer by m1vClock. Nothing was sent to the internet.

data.name: Diag.Report.Intro
data.value: The report stays on your computer only. Choose what to include, save or copy it and send it to whoever will help. Serial numbers, network addresses and the computer name are left out, unless you turn on the name option.

data.name: Diag.Report.IncludeName.Detail
data.value: Off by default, because the name can identify you.

data.name: Diag.Report.Preview
data.value: Preview of what goes in the report

data.name: Diag.Report.Preview.Empty
data.value: No part chosen. Turn on at least one above.

data.name: Opt.Startup.Intro
data.value: These programs start together with Windows and compete for processor, memory and disk right at sign-in. Turning one off does not uninstall anything, and you can turn it back on whenever you want.

data.name: Opt.Startup.NeedAdmin
data.value: Needs m1vClock as administrator to change this program.

data.name: Opt.Startup.Disable.Message
data.value: {0} stops opening on its own when you sign in to Windows. The program stays installed and works normally when you open it.

data.name: Opt.Startup.Disable.Change
data.value: The startup state of {0} becomes turned off.

data.name: Opt.Startup.Enable.Message
data.value: {0} starts opening on its own when you sign in to Windows.

data.name: Opt.Startup.Enable.Change
data.value: The startup state of {0} becomes turned on.

data.name: Opt.Startup.Undo
data.value: To go back, use the button here again or Undo on the History page.

data.name: Opt.Startup.Done.Disabled
data.value: {0} was turned off at startup. You can undo it on the History page.

data.name: Opt.Startup.Done.Enabled
data.value: {0} was turned on at startup. You can undo it on the History page.

data.name: Opt.Startup.NoRestorePoint
data.value: Warning: the restore point could not be created before the change ({0}).

data.name: Opt.Services.Intro
data.value: Services are programs that Windows and other programs keep running in the background. m1vClock only lets you change the startup of third-party services that are not antivirus or anti-cheat. The change applies from the next time the PC starts.

data.name: Opt.Services.Search
data.value: Search by name, company or description

data.name: Opt.Services.Summary.AutoThird
data.value: Third-party that start on their own

data.name: Opt.Services.Protection.Windows
data.value: Windows service: m1vClock does not change its startup.

data.name: Opt.Services.Protection.SecuritySoftware
data.value: Antivirus or security software: m1vClock does not change its startup.

data.name: Opt.Services.Protection.AntiCheat
data.value: Anti-cheat: turning it off can stop games from opening. m1vClock does not change its startup.

data.name: Opt.Services.Change.Message
data.value: {0} will start as {1} the next time the PC starts. The service is not stopped or started now.

data.name: Opt.Services.Change.Line

data.name: Opt.Services.Change.Undo

data.name: Opt.Services.ReadFailed

data.name: Opt.Services.Showing
data.value: Showing {0} of {1} services. Use the search to find the others.

data.name: Opt.Cleanup.Intro
data.value: Cleanup only touches folders from a fixed list, where Windows and programs recreate what they need. Only files older than a day are included, and whatever is in use stays. What gets deleted does not go to the recycle bin and cannot be undone.

data.name: Opt.Cleanup.Cat.userTemp.Detail
data.value: Leftovers from programs in the Temp folder, older than a day. Open programs may be using some, and those stay.

data.name: Opt.Cleanup.Cat.windowsTemp.Detail
data.value: The Windows Temp folder, with files older than a day.

data.name: Opt.Cleanup.Cat.updateDownloads.Detail
data.value: Updates that were already downloaded. Windows downloads them again if it needs to.

data.name: Opt.Cleanup.Cat.crashDumps.Detail
data.value: Files Windows keeps when a program crashes. They are for diagnosis only and can be large.

data.name: Opt.Cleanup.Cat.errorReports.Detail
data.value: Crash reports that were already archived or are queued.

data.name: Opt.Cleanup.Cat.shaderCache.Detail
data.value: Windows and games rebuild it on their own. The first game after cleaning may open a little slower.

data.name: Opt.Cleanup.NeedsAdmin.Tip
data.value: Open m1vClock as administrator to clean this place.

data.name: Opt.Cleanup.Confirm.Message
data.value: Deleted files do not go to the recycle bin and cannot be undone. Only those in the listed folders, older than a day and not in use are included.

data.name: Opt.Cleanup.Confirm.Undo
data.value: There is no way to undo it. If in doubt, cancel.

data.name: Opt.Cleanup.Done.Kept
data.value: {0} stayed because they are in use or protected.

data.name: Opt.Memory.Intro
data.value: Standby memory is a cache: Windows keeps there what was used recently so it opens again faster. It counts as free for programs, so there is almost never a reason to empty it. Emptying it does not touch the memory of open programs, but Windows will have to read the data from disk again, and for a moment everything may feel a little slower.

data.name: Opt.Memory.Modified
data.value: Modified, waiting to be written to disk: {0}

data.name: Opt.Memory.NeedsAdmin
data.value: Needs m1vClock as administrator to empty standby memory.

data.name: Opt.Memory.Confirm.Message
data.value: Only the Windows cache is discarded. The memory of your open programs is not touched, but recently used files may take a little longer to open.

data.name: Opt.Memory.Confirm.Line
data.value: About {0} of cache will be discarded.

data.name: Opt.Memory.Confirm.Undo
data.value: It cannot be undone, but Windows fills the cache again on its own.

data.name: Opt.Apps.Intro
data.value: This is the list of programs Windows has registered as installed, without system components. m1vClock deletes nothing here: the Uninstall button opens the program's own uninstaller, and it decides what to remove. Programs that did not report an uninstaller have no button.

data.name: Opt.Apps.Showing

data.name: Opt.Apps.ReadFailed

data.name: Opt.Apps.Confirm.Message
data.value: m1vClock will open the program's own uninstaller. It may ask for administrator permission, and it decides what to remove; m1vClock deletes nothing.

data.name: Opt.Apps.Confirm.Line

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.Intro
data.value: Small Windows tweaks for gaming. All of them can be turned off again, they only touch what each card describes, and none lowers Windows security: Defender, UAC, Windows Update and core isolation stay as they are. Before each change m1vClock shows what will be written, and Restore originals brings everything back to how it was before you used this page.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.UserNote
data.value: User tweaks apply to the account {0}.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.Issue.NoHighPerformancePlan
data.value: This Windows does not have the High performance plan, and m1vClock does not create power plans.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.Issue.NoPlanToReturnTo
data.value: There is no other power plan to go back to.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.Issue.ReadFailed
data.value: Could not read the state of this tweak.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.Change.Message

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.power.Description
data.value: Keeps the CPU ready to boost at once, without aggressive power saving.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.power.Effect
data.value: Fewer stutters in some games. On laptops it uses more battery. Turning it off returns to the plan that was active before.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.gamemode.Description
data.value: Gives the game priority and keeps Windows Update from installing or restarting during a match.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.gamemode.Effect
data.value: Recommended on: it is the Windows 11 default.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.gamedvr.Description
data.value: Turns off the Xbox Game Bar's continuous capture, which records the last minutes of gameplay all the time.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.gamedvr.Effect
data.value: Can recover a few FPS and reduce GPU and disk use. You lose the Game Bar's record-what-just-happened.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.hags.Description
data.value: The graphics card manages its own work queue instead of the CPU.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.hags.Effect
data.value: Required for DLSS 3 Frame Generation. May lower latency. Needs a compatible card and driver and a PC restart.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.windowed.Description
data.value: Makes DirectX 10 and 11 games in a window or borderless use the modern presentation model (flip).

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.windowed.Effect
data.value: Lower latency and VRR support in a window. A Windows 11 feature.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.mouse.Description
data.value: Unchecks Enhance pointer precision: the cursor always moves the same distance for the same movement.

data.name: Opt.Tweaks.mouse.Effect
data.value: Does not change FPS, but makes aim consistent in shooters. Takes effect at once.

data.name: Opt.Repair.Intro
data.value: Here m1vClock only checks. Nothing is repaired or changed: if a problem shows up, you get the command to run yourself. The checks need m1vClock as administrator, can take several minutes and can be cancelled. If you leave this page, the check in progress is cancelled.

data.name: Opt.Repair.NeedAdmin
data.value: Open m1vClock as administrator to run the checks.

data.name: Opt.Repair.Quick.Description
data.value: Reads only the problem flag Windows already stored about the component store, where it takes files from to repair and install features. Takes seconds.

data.name: Opt.Repair.Full.Description
data.value: Scans the whole component store for damaged files without fixing anything. Takes several minutes and uses the disk heavily.

data.name: Opt.Repair.Files.Description
data.value: Compares the protected Windows files with the stored copies and reports the ones that differ, without fixing anything. Takes several minutes.

data.name: Opt.Repair.Advice.Components
data.value: Windows flagged the component store as damaged. To repair it, open Terminal as administrator and run the command below, which needs internet. m1vClock does not do this repair yet.

data.name: Opt.Repair.Advice.Files
data.value: To repair, open Terminal as administrator and run the command below. m1vClock does not do this repair yet.

data.name: Opt.Repair.Advice.Failed
data.value: The check did not finish. The reason is in the app log.

data.name: Opt.Repair.Advice.FailedCode
data.value: The check did not finish (code {0}). The reason is in the app log.

data.name: Opt.Repair.CopyFailed
data.value: Could not copy. Select the command and copy it by hand.

data.name: Opt.Repair.Advice.FilesFound
data.value: SFC found system files that differ from the stored copies.

data.name: Opt.Repair.Advice.Trimmed
data.value: If your Windows was trimmed down on purpose, like Atlas, the repair may bring back what was removed.

data.name: Opt.Repair.Running.NoProgress
data.value: This check does not show its progress here. It usually takes a few minutes.
